newsitem.title: USA: CSX sets $220 million on Chicago rail link.
newsitem.headline: CSX sets $220 million on Chicago rail link.

text.p: CSX Corp. will spend about $220 million to improve and expand capacity on 270 miles of railroad between Greenwich, Ohio, and Chicago.

CSX Chief Executive John Snow said Monday the project will mean better service and vastly increased capacity across the line, which connects Cleveland, Boston, New York and Philadelphia with the industrial Midwest and Chicago.
Richmond, Va.-based CSX has interests in rail, container-shipping, trucking, barge and contract logistics services.
"This major construction project will create a truly world-class stretch of railroad with enormous economic potential, not only for CSX, but also for Ohio," Snow told a news conference.
Analysts said the move should benefit rail companies on either side of the Midwest because Chicago is the gateway connecting eastern rail lines with those in the West.
"It's one of the biggest cities for rail transportation," said Doug Rockel, rail analyst at Furman Selz. "Every major railroad interconnects with one another through Chicago."

CSX spokesman Tom Hoppin said the line, which carries about 20 to 25 trains a day, should carry about 50 trains a day when the project is completed in 1998. Ultimately, more than 100 miles of new track will be built and another 250 miles of existing track rebuilt and upgraded or surfaced.

Steven Lewins, a rail analyst at Gruntal & Co said the expansion is just one step of the CSX's efforts to digest the portion of Conrail that it is acquiring. CSX and Norfolk Southern Corp. agreed in March to acquire Conrail jointly in a $10.3 billion deal after a bitter takeover battle.
"In the greater scheme of things, it's just one piece in a very big puzzle that's going get put together in the next five years," Lewins said.
